I am 62 years old and have farmed this same 2.2 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My wife and I are the only two in our household, so we do all the labor ourselves. We cannot afford to take big risks or try fancy new methods. I know what works here: wheat in winter, maize in summer, on the same plot. It is autumn now, and the maize has just come off the field.

For my wheat this year, I will plant the full 2.2 mu with improved seed I buy from the village supply store. I do not save my own wheat seed anymore—the shop seed yields better. I will rotary till first to break up the stubble and make a good seedbed. At planting, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, about 50 kg. That gives me my phosphorus and potassium. Then at green-up in spring, I topdress with urea—about 20 kg per mu. I know it costs money, but two years ago I cut back and the wheat turned yellow, so I will not risk that again. I will irrigate four times: before winter freeze-up, at jointing, at heading, and once during grain filling if the weather stays dry. The well pump uses electricity, but wheat needs water to pay back. I will spray three times: herbicide once when the weeds first show in spring, and insecticide twice if the aphids or rust look bad. If the frost does not hit hard, I expect about 500 kg per mu.

For summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June—there is no time to waste. Because the window is so tight, I do not till; I plant directly into the wheat stubble, no-tillage. I buy hybrid seed, usually Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop recommends that year. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu, and a small topdress of urea later. Summer rains usually help, but I will irrigate twice if it turns dry, especially when the maize is at the big trumpet stage. I spray pesticide twice: herbicide when the maize is still small, and insecticide if I see armyworms. I expect around 560 kg per mu in a normal year.

I do not have much spare cash, and I am too old to chase every new technique. My neighbor Lao Wang cut his fertilizer last season and did fine, but his soil is different. On my land, I would rather spend a little too much and sleep easy than lose a whole season to thrift.
